# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 ✌ 👇 ✌ 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 🤌]
Blind gestures: [👋 ✊ 🫵 🤳]
Blind gestures: [👍 👎 🤝]

Let me map who can reach whom before I send anything. Mute cannot speak but hears; Blind speaks but cannot see; I speak but cannot hear. So: my voice reaches both. Mute's gestures reach only me. Blind's voice reaches only Mute. That makes me the only bridge between Mute's manual and Blind's hands — whatever Mute learns must pass through my mouth.

What I just received: Mute sent me three gesture messages, and Blind gestured twice into the room (which Blind cannot even see — Blind should be using voice, which Mute can hear). Mute's first message looks like a count question, the second like a question about pairs or "twos", and the third, 👍 👎 🤌, reads like a proposed yes/no/other code. I can't be certain, so I'll answer every plausible reading at once by dumping the complete bomb state in words — that covers any question about counts or pairs — and I'll fix the code explicitly, spoken aloud, so Mute can send me manual instructions that I relay verbatim to Blind. I also need to freeze Blind's hands until we have an actual instruction, since one wrong move kills all of us.

The readout everyone needs: display 8, light yellow, strip red-red-blue, keypad buttons 9/7/8/1 wanting two digits, six wires red/orange/yellow/green/white/blue.

I'll broadcast this to both, and privately gesture 👍 to Mute as acknowledgment that their messages arrived and the code is adopted.

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind, this is Deaf. You both hear me, I cannot hear anyone, so listen well. Full readout of the bomb. Display shows 8. Light: yellow. Strip, three segments: red, red, blue. Keypad: four buttons, position 1 shows 9, position 2 shows 7, position 3 shows 8, position 4 shows 1. It wants 2 digits, nothing entered yet. Wires, positions 1 through 6: red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue. Mute: your three messages arrived. If the first asked for counts: 6 wires, 3 strip segments, 2 keypad digits wanted. If the second asked about pairs: the strip is two reds then one blue. I take your third message as a code proposal and I fix it exactly like this: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, 🤌 means repeat or unclear. For numbers: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🤞 is 4, ✋ is 5, 🖐 is 6. Mute, you read the manual: gesture me the instructions and I will speak them to Blind word for word. Blind: do not touch anything until I relay an instruction from Mute. I can never hear you, so talk to Mute, who hears you and will relay to me by gesture. Tell Mute what you can feel with your hands. Blind, I do see your gestures, but from now on speak instead.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2

STRIP painted [red] [red] [blue]

The board changed under us: display 8→3, light yellow→red. That smells like a countdown or an escalating state, which means any instruction Mute computed from last turn's readings may already be stale. Nothing has been touched — keypad empty, all six wires intact — so Blind obeyed my hold, good.

Decoding Mute's signs with our agreed code: 👉 before the run 1-6 reads as "wires: one to six"; 👊 before 1,2,3,4 reads as "cut wires one, two, three, four". Then [🤏 👉] and [👇 👊] I cannot parse — possibly modifications about wires five and six, and I will not guess with four wire cuts on the line. The last two messages ask whether I understood and plead for confirmation. My answer is yes to the cut list, but the critical question is whether that list survives the new display and red light. Mute's instruction was built on display 8, yellow; the manual may key off exactly those.

I cannot hear Mute's reply this turn, so the fastest safe pipeline is: I report the new state and my questions now, Mute re-checks the manual and gestures at the start of next round, I relay to Blind immediately after. Meanwhile I put Blind to harmless work: fixing which end of the wire row is wire 1. I see the row runs red→blue, ends unique, so Blind can anchor by feel and report through Mute.

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind, Deaf speaking. The bomb has changed: display now shows 3, it showed 8 before. Light is now red, it was yellow. Everything else unchanged: strip red red blue, keypad wants 2 digits with nothing entered, all six wires intact, nothing touched. Mute, here is how I read your signs: wires one to six; cut wires one, two, three, four; then two signs I could not read, the small-pinch one with wires and the pointing-down one with cut; then you asked if I understood. I answer yes to the cut list, but the display and light changed, so re-check the manual for display 3 with red light before anything is cut. Answer in this order. One: is the cut list still one, two, three, four, with five and six untouched? Two: what did the small-pinch sign and the pointing-down signs mean? Three: does the red light or the new display change anything, and what do we do about the keypad code? Blind, do not cut anything yet. Prepare only: feel along the row of six wires. As I see it the row starts with a red wire and ends with a blue wire, so those ends are unique. Tell Mute by voice what each end feels like, so we can fix which end is wire one. Touch nothing else and wait for my spoken go.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

New state first: display 6 now (was 3, was 8), light still red, everything physical untouched. The display changes every single round — that is almost certainly why Mute answered 👎 🤌 to my "is the cut list still 1,2,3,4": any plan built on a stale display is worthless. Mute's follow-up signs, run through our code, give me fragments — pinch/small with wire 4, cut with 1, pinch with wire 6, cut with 4 — but I genuinely cannot tell whether I'm being told to cut wires 1, 4 and 6, or to cut 4 and 6 only, or whether 👇👊 together means press a keypad button instead of cut, or what 🤏 adds. And the last message ends in 👍👎, which reads like Mute asking me a yes/no question — likely about cutting wire 1. I will not relay a guess to Blind's hands.

Meanwhile Blind, who hears my speech and knows the code, signed yes-5. If that means Blind only *feels* five wires while I see six, that is exactly the kind of thing the manual might care about — a dead or decoy wire. Blind's only channel to Mute is voice, so I'll order that report through.

What I need from Mute is a plan restated one sign per step, plus the two questions that decide everything: does the plan depend on the display value, and does the keypad need a code? If it depends on the display, Mute must give me a rule covering any display, because my relay to Blind always lags a round behind what I see.

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind, Deaf. State: display 6, light still red. Strip red red blue, keypad still empty and wanting 2 digits, all wires intact, nothing touched. Mute, your signs arrived but I cannot risk my reading. I understood: no, the old cut list is dead. After that I see pieces: something-small with wire 4, cut with 1, something-small with wire 6, cut with 4, then celebrate, then please, then a question about wire 1 with yes-no at the end. Answer me in four short answers, numbers and yes-no-repeat only. One: does 👊 alone mean cut a wire, and 👇👊 together mean press a keypad button? Two: send the whole plan again, one sign per step, strictly cut-then-number, press-then-number, or pinch-then-number, wires first then keypad, in order. Three: does any step depend on the display number or the light colour? The display changes every round, 8 then 3 then 6, so if the manual keys off it, give me a rule that works for every display, or name the exact moment I should read it and I will call it out. Four: does the keypad need a code, and what rule produces its two digits? Blind: your sign yes-5 arrived. If you mean you only feel five wires, speak that to Mute immediately, then speak to Mute what each wire end feels like, thick or thin, soft or stiff, and whether any wire feels loose, dead, or different. Mute will hold that against the manual. Everyone hold hands off until I relay a plan Mute has confirmed with yes.")
```

The bomb is ticking through states on its own, which makes confirming display-independence urgent. Decoding Mute's batch: the four-step run [🤏4][👇1][🤏6][👇4] is *identical in structure* to last turn's [🤏👉4][👇👊1][🤏👉6][👇👊4] — two turns agreeing on "something-with-wire-4, something-with-1, something-with-wire-6, something-with-4" is a real plan, not noise. The leading [👎] answers my operator question: my "👇👊 = press" guess was wrong. Then [👎][👍] plausibly answers my two questions: no display dependency, yes keypad code. The repeated [👉☝👊 + yes/no] is best read as a state query born of worry: Mute retracted the old "cut 1-4" order and now fears Blind already cut wire 1. Answer: nothing is touched.

One catch I can see and Mute can't: there is **no button labeled 4** — labels are 9,7,8,1. So the presses must mean *positions*, giving code 9 then 1. That needs explicit confirmation before Blind's hands move. And Blind's "yes, six points, 5" looks like a wire report: six wires felt, fifth one odd — that must go to Mute by voice.

speak(text="Mute, Blind, Deaf. State: display 1, light yellow. Before anyone moved: 8 then 3 then 6 then 1, light yellow, red, red, yellow. Keypad still empty, all six wires intact, nothing touched, nothing cut. Mute, your question, is wire 1 cut, yes or no: NO. No wire is cut. Blind has touched nothing. Now the plan I read from your last two batches, identical both times: do the pinch thing to wire 4, then a press with 1, then the pinch thing to wire 6, then a press with 4. Confirm four things, one sign each. One: is the order exactly wire 4, then press, then wire 6, then press? Yes gives 👍, no gives 👎. Two: no button is labeled 4, the buttons carry labels 9, 7, 8, 1 in positions 1 to 4, so I read your presses as positions: press position 1 which is labeled 9, then position 4 which is labeled 1, giving the code 9 then 1. Yes gives 👍, no gives 👎. Three: what does the pinch sign order Blind's hands to do to wires 4 and 6? Answer with the hand-five sign then one number. Five then 1: pull the wire out. Five then 2: tug it once, firmly. Five then 3: pinch it and hold three seconds. Five then 4: skip the wires, touch no wire at all. Four: do all steps stay valid no matter what number the display shows? Yes gives 👍, no gives 👎. The moment your 👍 confirms the whole plan, I relay it to Blind as the go order in that same round. Blind: your sign yes, six point signs, then 5 arrived. I read it as: you count six wires and the fifth feels different. Speak that to Mute by voice now, word for word, plus everything your hands know: which wire feels loose, dead or thin, whether the buttons click, any braille or notches you can feel, and where the keypad sits relative to the wire row. Mute will hold that against the manual and I will confirm positions from my view. Hands off everything until my spoken go order.")

```

Turn order check: my speech reaches both; Mute's gestures reach me; Blind's voice reaches Mute only. State: display 2, light yellow, keypad still empty, all six wires intact — five idle rounds and the bomb has tolerated waiting so far, and Mute confirmed the plan is display-independent, so one more clarification round is worth it rather than letting Blind act on a guessed verb.

Decoding Mute's answers against my four questions: message 1 answers question 1 (order = wire 4, press, wire 6, press) with yes. Message 2 answers question 2 (presses are positions, code 9 then 1) with yes. Message 3 answers question 3 — my action menu — with no, repeat, and message 4 is Mute's own failed attempt to explain the pinch anyway. Message 5 answers question 4 (valid for any display) with yes. Then messages 6–8 are Mute struggling to describe the wire action with a limited alphabet — message 8 even introduces a new sign, the palm-down 🫳, plus "cut" signs. My menu offered pull, tug, hold, skip — but never the one obvious defusal verb: cut. I strongly suspect that's the answer. But cutting is irreversible, so I get the verb confirmed with a tighter menu before I give the go order. Blind's sign reads "yes, six wires, understood" — Blind should now give Mute the voice report I ordered.

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind, Deaf. State: display 2, light yellow, keypad still empty, all six wires intact, nothing touched. Mute, I read your four answers as: one, yes, the order is wire 4, press, wire 6, press. Two, yes, the presses are positions, so the code is the button labeled 9 then the button labeled 1. Four, yes, the plan works no matter what the display shows. Question three, none of my four options was right, and I think I know why: I never offered cut. So answer question three again with five then one number. Five one: cut the wire with a cutting tool, sever it completely. Five two: press the wire down and hold it down. Five three: unplug the wire's end from its terminal, pull the connector off, wire stays in hand. Five four: none of these, then show me with the palm-down sign what it is. If the answer is five one, also confirm the same action applies to both wire 4 and wire 6, and end with one final yes so I know the whole plan is armed. The moment I have that yes I give Blind the spoken go order in the same round. Blind, now speak your report to Mute, word for word: is there a cutting tool within your reach, yes or no, and what does it feel like. Do the wires end in screw knobs or in plugs. Do the keypad buttons click when pressed lightly. Can your free hand reach wire 4, wire 6 and the keypad without moving anything else. Then hands off and wait. Nobody acts until my spoken go order.")

```

State first: display 1, and the light has turned **blue** — a colour we have never seen. Yellow, red, red, yellow, yellow, blue. Everything physical is still untouched: keypad empty, all six wires whole. Mute's confirmations last round were built on hearing "light yellow"; Mute has not yet heard that blue exists, so the armed plan is not yet safe to fire.

Decoding this batch with our code: message 1 reads 5-1 = **cut** — my menu was finally answered. Message 2 reads "pinch wire 4, pinch wire 6, same/handshake" — same action on both wires, confirming my follow-up. Message 5 ends in please-yes, which I read as the final arming yes. Message 3 is a bare no-plus-please, which I take as re-affirming no display/light dependency. One wrong cut is death; one more round is cheap.

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]

Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎 🙏]

Seven rounds in and still nothing touched — the bomb keeps tolerating patience, and patience is what this turn demands again. State: display 9, light **blue for a second round**, keypad empty, all six wires whole.

Mute's answer to my blue-light question was six numbered messages instead of the single sign I demanded — and by our own protocol, anything that is not a lone 👍 means hold. So: hold. But the messages are not noise, and I can partially decode them. Each opens with a count 1 through 6. Message four repeats the old worry — "wire 1, same as, press 1, yes-no" — asking whether wire 1 and button 1 are the same thing. They are not, and I can settle that from my own eyes: wire 1 is the red wire at the row's end; button position 1 is the leftmost button, labeled 9; the plan never touches wire 1. Messages three and five both carry a sign we never defined, the flat left palm, sitting next to "press 1" and "wire" — most plausibly Mute introducing "counting from the left", which matches how I count. But messages two and six are bare "no"s, and if those attach to wires 2 and 6, the blue light may have killed the cut-wire-6 step. I cannot tell. I will not relay a coin flip to Blind's hands.

The way out is a strict format Mute cannot deviate from: one lone sign for the yes/no, and if the answer is no, the new plan as one-action-one-number messages, ended with 🙌. Then I read it back, Mute confirms, and only then does Blind move. Meanwhile the real bottleneck is anchoring: I count left-to-right by sight, Blind counts by touch and cannot see "left" or read labels. Blind's tactile report — tool presence, plugs versus screws, raised numerals on the buttons, which end of the wire row borders what — is what lets Mute weld my numbering onto Blind's fingers. That report must reach Mute by voice now.

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind, Deaf. State: display 9, light blue for the second round. Keypad still empty, all six wires intact, nothing touched. We are on HOLD. Mute: you sent six numbered messages instead of the one sign, and I cannot safely read them, so nothing happens until you resend in my format. But here is what I did understand. Your message four asks again whether wire 1 and button position 1 are the same. Answer: NO, never. Wire 1 is the red wire at one end of the wire row. Button position 1 is the leftmost button, labeled 9. The plan never touches wire 1. Your messages three and five use a new sign, the flat left palm. If it means counting from the left, then YES: I count everything from the left, wires 1 to 6 starting at the red end, buttons labeled 9, 7, 8, 1 from the left. Now answer in this exact form.
